name: How to Prepare for a Ground-Up Bathroom Addition Project

step.name: Step 1: Confirm available space and evaluate existing structure
step.text: Measure your intended footprint and inspect the subfloor, joists, and nearby plumbing stacks. Ensure the floor framing can support wet fixtures and that there is adequate vertical drop for waste lines.

step.name: Step 2: Create detailed layouts and fixture placement plans
step.text: Draw scaled plans showing exact locations for the toilet, vanity, shower or tub, lighting, ground-fault protected outlets, and ventilation. Verify required clearance measurements between fixtures before finalizing the design.

step.name: Step 3: Secure required building, plumbing, and electrical permits
step.text: Submit your plans to the local building department to secure necessary approvals before cutting into walls or floors. Professional contractors help coordinate this paperwork so rough work passes official scrutiny without unexpected delays.

step.name: Step 4: Complete rough framing, plumbing, and electrical installations
step.text: Frame the partition walls, run supply and drain lines, rough in exhaust venting directly to the exterior, and set dedicated electrical circuits. Schedule all necessary rough-in municipal inspections before closing up any wall cavities.

step.name: Step 5: Apply proper waterproofing systems and hang moisture-resistant drywall
step.text: Install cement backer board or specialized waterproof membranes in shower and tub zones to block water intrusion. Hang moisture-resistant drywall across remaining wall areas and prepare all joints for a clean finish.

step.name: Step 6: Install tile, trim, fixtures, and final finishes
step.text: Lay tile flooring and shower surrounds, mount vanities, secure plumbing trim, install GFCI receptacles, and complete interior paint. Schedule final building and trade inspections to verify the addition is safe and fully compliant.
